label: feature
title: Configurable timeouts for InferenceGraph
text:
InferenceServices in a Serverless deployment of KServe allow you to configure the Knative `timeoutSeconds` field by way of the `timeout` field in ComponentExtensionSpec. We'd like the same feature for an InferenceGraph.

If we cannot update the InfereceGraph spec at this time, I would request the InferenceGraph controller at the very least be able to check the existing InferenceServices for Knative-backed components and match the highest `timeoutSeconds`.

Thanks for your consideration!

label: feature
title: Support overriding model mount path in model server container
text:
Currently it is not possible to specify at what path the downloaded model should be available in the model server container. The downloaded model is always mounted in the model server container at `/mnt/models`. 

We should allow the user to specify the path inside the model server container the volume should be mounted at. e.g.

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  annotations:
    ds.bloomberg.com/gpuSubtype: bloomberg.com/gpu-l4
    identities.bloomberg.com/bcs: platform-bcosv2
  name: huggingface-t5-hfs
  namespace: s-dsplatform
spec:
  predictor:
    containers:
      - --model
      - llama-2-70b
      - --num_gpus=4
      command:
      - nemollm_inference_ms
      env:
      - name: STORAGE_URI
        value: s3://models/llama-7b
      - name: STORAGE_MOUNT_PATH
        value: /model-store
      image: nvcr.io/ohlfw0olaadg/ea-participants/nim_llm:24.02
```

Since serving runtimes may require models to be mounted at a specific location we should also make it configurable on a runtime level. e.g.

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: nim
spec:
  containers:
    - nemollm_inference_ms
    image: nvcr.io/ohlfw0olaadg/ea-participants/nim_llm:24.02
    name: kserve-container
    ports:
    - containerPort: 9999
      protocol: TCP
  modelMountPath: /model-store
  supportedModelFormats:
  - autoSelect: true
    name: nim
```

label: feature
title: Get `response_code` metrics for gRPC calls and requests
text:
I have just implemented [Queue Proxy Extension](https://github.com/alexagriffith/kserve/tree/master/qpext) as a sidecar container to replace queue-proxy, and get more metrics from it. I noticed that `revision_app_request_count` focuses on HTTP only requests.

When using gRPC to reach an `InferenceService`, the `revision_app_request_count` reports always successful calls (response code in `2xx`) even when gRPC calls are failing. Even if gRPC uses HTTP under the hood, it would be useful to get a metric with the errors.

It would be nice to have a metric to observe the success and error rate of gRPC calls too. I am not sure if reusing `revision_app_request_count` metric is a good idea over using a brand new one from kserve container itself, but the idea is to be able to measure it from kserve.

label: bug
title: KServe RestServer Disabling Other Customized Module Level Loggings
text:
We have used our own module level loggings but no log from our code will show up. Our logs are likely to be suppressed by this part of the [code](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/389659a0c5067d2086cf960dcb1149d676254025/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/server.py#L141-L176) where `disable_existing_loggers=False` is not included. Since this value is defaulted to be `True` according to the [document](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.config.html#logging-config-dictschema) of logging . Omitting this will disable every other logger but just keep the kserve *rest server ones*.

Our customized module level loggings to show up.

A one line change of adding  `disable_existing_loggers=False` between [code](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/389659a0c5067d2086cf960dcb1149d676254025/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/server.py#L141-L176) might be able to fix this. Also we might want to use module level logger in `model_server` [here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/389659a0c5067d2086cf960dcb1149d676254025/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L63) according to [logging library documentation which suggests not using root logger](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/logging.html#configuring-logging-for-a-library) just like the used uvicorn server [logger](https://github.com/encode/uvicorn/blob/master/uvicorn/server.py#L34). Thank you!

label: feature
title: Native integration with KEDA for LLM inference autoscaling
text:
To autoscale LLM inference services Knative's request level metrics may not be the best scaling metrics as LLM inference is performed at the token level and we need to understand the number of input/output tokens to scale. To effectively autoscale LLM inference services, we'd like to scale based on metrics like token throughput, power consumption. 

In order to achieve this Autoscaler needs to be able to query metrics from prometheus. KEDA supports [scaling based on prometheus metrics](https://keda.sh/docs/1.4/scalers/prometheus/) and we would like to implement a native integration with KEDA for both serverless and raw deployment mode to support autoscaling LLM inference out of the box.

A few important metrics:
* Time To First Token (TTFT): Low waiting times for a response are essential in real-time interactions, but less important in offline workloads.
* Time Per Output Token (TPOT): Time to generate an output token for each user that is querying our system. This metric corresponds with how each user will perceive the "speed" of the model.
* Latency: The overall time it takes for the model to generate the full response for a user. Overall response latency can be calculated using the previous two metrics: latency = (TTFT) + (TPOT) * (the number of tokens to be generated). 
* Throughput: The number of output tokens per second an inference server can generate across all users and requests. 
* Power consumption: Metrics produced by [Kepler](https://github.com/sustainable-computing-io/kepler), e.g kepler_container_joules_total.

- Knative has a PoC to integrate with KEDA and @skonto is [creating a new repo](https://github.com/knative/community/issues/1527) for `serving-keda` under knative-extensions org.
- For Raw Deployment mode we can provision the `ScalerObject` in kserve controller and allow user to specify the metrics query on `InferenceService` spec. 

```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "llama2-vllm"
spec:
  predictor:
    scaleQuery: "average_token_throughput_per_second[1m]"
    scaleMetric: custom
    maxReplicas: 10
    minReplicas: 1
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: huggingface
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/huggingface/llama2-70b"
```

```yaml
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaleObject
metadata:
  name: llama2-vllm-scaleobject
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: llama2-vllm-deployment
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 30
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 10
  triggers:
    - type: prometheus
      metadata:
        serverAddress: http://prometheus-server
        metricName: average_token_per_second
        query: average_token_per_second[1m]
        threshold: "500"
```

[Optional, start with the short-form [RFC template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UcBeLfZ_JMGpVrPJmYtEIVH_9Y4U3AEKQdq_IKuOMrU) to outline your ideas and get early feedback.]
[Required, use the longer-form [design doc template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Mtoui_PP2a9N59NjYHnsvrdJ8t2iKFwIJAx1zRO_I1c) to specify and discuss your design in more detail]

label: bug
title: 'AioServer.shutdown' was never awaited for kserve fastapi server
text:
Create a simple kserve model:
```
import kserve
from typing import Dict
import argparse
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class CustomModel(kserve.Model):
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        super().__init__(name)
        self.name = name
        self.load()

    def load(self):
        self.ready = True

    def predict(self,request: Dict, headers: Dict ) -> Dict:
        logger.info(request)
        return request

DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME = "custom-model"

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(parents=[kserve.model_server.parser])
parser.add_argument('--model_name', default=DEFAULT_MODEL_NAME,
                    help='The name that the model is served under.')

args, _ = parser.parse_known_args()
if __name__ == "__main__":
    model = CustomModel(name=args.model_name)
    kserve.ModelServer().start([model])
```
And when you run the server:
```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
sys:1: RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'AioServer.shutdown' was never awaited
```

What worked for me is adding this line before initializing the model:
```
multiprocessing.set_start_method('fork')
```

The above issue only happens on mac, and does not seem to happen with linux containers, this is probably something to do with how to OS defaults to creating new processes.

label: feature
title: Enhance manager setup based on available CRDs
text:
This issue specifically refers to the code of this func: https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/99ac7b2050fafb14b7114b94ad6e3fd7ecfe3d15/pkg/controller/v1beta1/inferenceservice/controller.go#L298

Despite the KServe website has instructions to setup KServe under a Serverless environment and also under Raw, the manager setup uses configs to decide what set of CRDs are going to be watched.

Specifically, the decisions around the default deployment mode are not optimal. Users may still prefer using RawDeployment by default while using Serverless mode for the workloads where KNative-related features are needed. However, configuring RawDeployment as the default mode will lead to not watching KNative and Istio related resources, which is probably not OK because users may modify them and break the setup and the controller won't fix the broken resources.

Therefore, rather than using the default deployment mode as a helper to set what resources to watch, it may be better to resolve if the CRDs are available to watch them. In case the user configures Serverless as default deployment mode, the controller would still run fine (right now it continuously restarts because of the missing CRDs) if the user has the policy to annotate all the ISVCs with RawDeployment mode and, if the annotation is forgotten, the manager would start logging errors and that would be fine.

label: bug
title: KServe KEDA autoscaler creates invalid HPA (averageUtilization: 0) and invalid CPU metric value when using Prometheus trigger
text:
When deploying an InferenceService with `autoscalerClass: "keda"` and a Prometheus metric trigger (following the [[official KServe KEDA autoscaler guide](https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/predictive-inference/autoscaling/keda-autoscaler/)](https://kserve.github.io/website/docs/model-serving/predictive-inference/autoscaling/keda-autoscaler/)), KServe creates a ScaledObject that fails to generate a valid HPA.

The resulting error message is:

```
failed to ensure HPA is correctly created for ScaledObject: HorizontalPodAutoscaler.autoscaling "keda-hpa-qwen3-single-node-predictor" is invalid: spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization: Invalid value: 0: must be greater than 0
```

---

* **KServe version:** v0.15.0 (Helm install)
* **KEDA version:** v2.15.0 (Helm install)
* **Kubernetes version:** v1.30
* **Deployment mode:** Standard (not RawDeployment)
* **Prometheus setup:** kube-prometheus-stack Helm chart
* **Runtime:** vLLM (custom ClusterServingRuntime)

---

1. Deploy the following InferenceService:

   ```yaml
   apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
   kind: InferenceService
   metadata:
     name: qwen3-single-node
     namespace: sunny
     annotations:
       serving.kserve.io/deploymentMode: "Standard"
       serving.kserve.io/autoscalerClass: "keda"
   spec:
     predictor:
       minReplicas: 1
       maxReplicas: 5
       model:
         modelFormat:
           name: huggingface
         runtime: vllm-single-node-rocm
         storageUri: pvc://models-nfs-pvc/Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct
       autoScaling:
         metrics:
           - type: External
             external:
               metric:
                 backend: "prometheus"
                 serverAddress: "http://kube-prometheus-stack-prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090"
                 query: vllm:num_requests_running
               target:
                 type: Value
                 value: "2"
   ```

2. Observe the ScaledObject and HPA creation.

---

* A ScaledObject is created, but the corresponding HPA creation fails with:

  ```
  spec.metrics[0].resource.target.averageUtilization: Invalid value: 0: must be greater than 0
  ```
* Adding a CPU resource metric resolves that particular error, but then the ScaledObject generates an invalid CPU utilization value (`824671889656`), causing another failure:

  ```
  error parsing cpu metadata: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "824671889656": value out of range
  ```
* When I manually edit that value in the deployed ScaledObject YAML, the HPA is created and autoscaling works.

---

KServe should:

* Generate a valid ScaledObject and HPA when only a Prometheus metric is used for scaling.
* Omit any CPU metric or default `averageUtilization` value if not explicitly defined.

---

* The Prometheus metric (`vllm:num_requests_running`) resolves correctly and returns non-zero values.
* The ServiceMonitor configuration is correct, and Prometheus shows the metric as expected.
* The KEDA team has confirmed this integration is managed on the KServe/Knative side.
* This issue may originate from the logic in KServe that generates the ScaledObject spec when using the KEDA autoscaler class.

label: bug
title: Runtime selection becomes unpredictable when two different priority is specified for the same model in a servingruntime
text:
When we specify two different priority for the same modelFormat with different versions,  the runtime selection becomes unpredictable. 

For example, Here is two serving runtimes. The MLServer runtime specifies two different priority for the 'sklearn' model with different version. At the same time Kserve sklearn runtime also has support for the 'sklearn' model with priority of 1.

Note: The runtimes are truncated for brevity.

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-mlserver
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
    - name: sklearn
      version: "0"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 1
    - name: sklearn
      version: "1"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 2
```
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: ClusterServingRuntime
metadata:
  name: kserve-sklearnserver
spec:
  supportedModelFormats:
    - name: sklearn
      version: "1"
      autoSelect: true
      priority: 1
```
When we apply the following yaml , The MLServer runtime should be selected as it has the higher priority which is 2. But instead Kserve Sklearn runtime is selected.

```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "sklearn-iris"
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: sklearn
      protocolVersion: "v2"
      storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model" 
```
This is due to the fact that MLServer has two different priorities and one of which is lower i.e. 1. We didn't specify the model version in the isvc, so three of the model formats are valid for this isvc. 

When the runtime is sorted by the supported model's priority at first MLserver  precedes  the Sklearn because of the modelformat with priority value of 2. At the second round Sklearn gets the precedence because of mlserver's modelformat with priority value of 1.

The MLServer runtime should be selected. 

We should add a validation for this edge case.

- KServe Version: 0.11.1
- Cloud Environment:[k8s_istio/istio_dex/gcp_basic_auth/gcp_iap/aws/aws_cognito/ibm]

I was able to [find this example](https://github.com/lampajr/model-registry-storage-initializer), however it was unclear about the suggested usage with mlflow.

label: feature
title: Add minBatchSize to batcher
text:
Currently the batcher waits for maxBatchSize before it sends instances to prediction. That means that if we exceed maxBatchSize, it will send more than maxBatchSize. That is somehow confusing as we send more than maxBatchSize for prediction.

Suggest to add an option to limit the max instances being sent to maxBatchSize. That can be done by defining two variables:

Wait for min batch size before sending to prediction
No more than max batch size will be sent to prediction (maxBatchSize > minBatchSize).

label: bug
title: Huggingface models are unusable
text:
This is related to #5299 . Due to that issue, it is impossible to modify the initContainer. Consequently, because of https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface_hub/issues/3300 attempting to download any model larger than 8Gb will cause an OOM error. This effectively makes HF models unusable in KServe 0.17 because init containers cannot be changed and the default initContainer is incompatible with the behavior of the huggingface_hub library.

The model downloads properly and runs.

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: LLMInferenceService
metadata:
  name: qwen3.5-35b-a3b-single
spec:
  model:
    uri: hf://Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
    name: Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
  template:
    containers:
      - name: main
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: '4'
            memory: 32Gi
            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
          requests:
            cpu: '2'
            memory: 16Gi
            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8000
            scheme: HTTPS
          initialDelaySeconds: 120
          periodSeconds: 30
          timeoutSeconds: 30
          failureThreshold: 5
```

The PR opened to fix the linked issue would enable a workaround, but the default initContainer limits should still be adjusted.

label: feature
title: Download files from Azure storage under virtual directory for Multi-model serving
text:
I propose implementing a feature to enable the downloading of all files from Azure storage under a specified virtual directory. This enhancement would facilitate the utilization of Multi-model serving capabilities.

The feature should support the downloading of files structured under a virtual directory in the following format:

```
azure://myStorageAccount.blob.core.windows.net/myContainer/my/Virtual/Dir/modelName
```
Under this structure, the files are organized as follows:

```
[config.pbtxt]
<version>/
  <model-definition-file>
<version>/
  <model-definition-file>
...
```
This enhancement would streamline the process of retrieving files from Azure storage for multi-model serving scenarios.

label: question
title: shared auth with kubeflow
text:
I've installed kubeflow from kfctl with a setup that [includes auth on the single external entrypoint for istio](https://www.kubeflow.org/docs/started/k8s/kfctl-existing-arrikto/).

But KFServices are available without any security on port 80. This is because knative and kubeflow both create an istio [Gateway resource](https://istio.io/docs/reference/config/networking/v1alpha3/gateway/) and the kubeflow entry doesn't include port 80 whereas knative does. So port 80 traffic is unsecured (and still open because not covered by the kubeflow auth envoyfilter) and is routed by istio to the knative services as it matches the knative gateway record.

I can move the knative gateway to the default https port but then there's a conflict with the kubeflow gateway and requests do not get routed to the services. The only configuration I've able to get working with auth is putting the knative gateway on a different port entirely (e.g. 15443). I suspect it would also work if I were to create [a distinct entrypoint IP for knative](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/setting-up-custom-ingress-gateway/), though that would require additional changes to the auth setup (to allow that redirectUri).

@yanniszark [has suggested](https://github.com/kubeflow/kfserving/issues/196#issuecomment-506827346) this could be addressed by getting knative to use the kubeflow gateway. But I've tried to do that without success. Knative lets you [repoint to a different external gateway service](https://knative.dev/docs/serving/setting-up-custom-ingress-gateway/) but I've not been able to point to a different isitio Gateway (changing the config-istio configmap didn't work for me).

I've also considered changing kubeflow to use the knative-gateway but that would be a big change.

label: feature
title: Add request encoder/decoder in Explainer model wrapper
text:
general description:
(correct me if I am wrong)

Model Explainer currently supports LIME as its default explainer engine, the very beginning requests will hit the [`explain()`](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/aixexplainer/aixserver/model.py#L51) API with an HTTP request when you send a request to the explainer endpoint (usually with the following format http://istio-ingressgateway.istio-system/v1/models/<model-name>:explain bundled with Kubeflow installation), and then the explainer will do its magic by perturbing the input data and sent them to the predictor with the API [`_predict()`](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/aixexplainer/aixserver/model.py#L44)

so the flow would look like this:
HTTP request  ---> explainer endpoint ---> predictor endpoint

In the current explainer ([aixexplainer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/aixexplainer/aixserver/model.py)), it decodes the request body into NumPy.array in `explain` API call https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/aixexplainer/aixserver/model.py#L73:

```
        try:
            inputs = np.array(instances[0])
            logging.info("Calling explain on image of shape %s", (inputs.shape,))
        except Exception as err:
```
and converting the tensor back to HTTP requests in `_predict` API calls 

```
        scoring_data = {'instances': input_im.tolist()}

        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        resp = loop.run_until_complete(self.predict(scoring_data))
        return np.array(resp["predictions"])
```

https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/aixexplainer/aixserver/model.py#L45

Using list of tensor is reasonable because the very beginning requests are sent with a list of tensors in the MNIST example
```
input_image = {"instances": [inputs.tolist()]}
input_image.update(parameters)
print("Sending Explain Query")
```
https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/samples/explanation/aix/mnist/query_explain.py#L50

However, to be a more general purpose of usage, a proper encoder/decoder should be introduced to mitigate the different formats of sending to the predictor, one of the examples is the flower example which is widely used in the e2e test (https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/samples/v1beta1/tensorflow/tensorflow.yaml#L8)

The Flower example is a good example to demonstrate how a proper encoder/decoder is required as the input looks differently from the MNIST example, the flower payload is defined below:
```
{
  "instances": [
    {
      "image_bytes": {"b64": <b64-string>}, 
      "key": <string>,
    }
  ]
}
```

As the requests should come with the same request format for one particular model, instead of detecting request codec dynamically, it make sense if we can determine the encoder/decoder format during the construction phase:

```
class AIXModel(kserve.Model):  # pylint:disable=c-extension-no-member
    def __init__(self, name: str, ..., request_encode_decoder: str):
```
then we construct the `request_encode_decoder` accordingly, beflow is a simple contracts of request codec for reference.

```
class AIXRequestEncodeDecoder():
  def Encode(input_im: np.ndarray):
    // coverting numpy.array into a HTTP requests to predictor
  def Decode(self, request:Dict):
    // converting the HTTP requerst into numpy.array
```

just want to hear your feedback and I got some bandwidth if you need more hands on this.

No

label: bug
title: Add ability to InferenceGraph to passTrough custom annotations
text:
Created a InferenceGraph with custom annotation: `custom.annotation/hostname: xxx` this annotaton is not propagated to downstream Knative service.

Expect this annotation to be propagated to downstream KNative Service

```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1
kind: InferenceGraph
metadata:
  annotations:
    custom.annotation/hostname: test
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: test
  name: test
  namespace: default
spec:
  nodes:
    root:
      routerType: Sequence
      steps:
        - name: test-transformer
          serviceName: test-transformer
        - data: $response
          name: test-predictor
          serviceName: test-predictor
```

There is a precedence for passthrough annotation `serving.knative.openshift.io/enablePassthrough: 'true'` That is explicitly passed [here](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/56b8fe0d189fc0d557e9a8af07eab0c12852d5fd/pkg/controller/v1alpha1/inferencegraph/knative_reconciler.go#L163)

This ability to pass annotations is convenient because it allows to dynamically generate dns records using tools such as external-dns on istio `virtualService`

label: feature
title: Propose new storage spec to support next-gen multi-model serving
text:
We want to introduce a new storage spec for inference service and trained model, so it can support the next-gen model mesh multi-model serving with different storage provider. The storageUri can continue to work with this new storage spec.
Example:
```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: example-sklearn-isvc

spec:
  predictor:
    sklearn:
      storage:

        path: sklearn/mnist-svm.joblib
        parameters:

```

label: feature
title: [Proposal] Decouple the model "fetch mechanism" from the internal storage field in the CRD
text:
Currently, the [`storage` field](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/6a824724aed4a1ffcca4623719858a83460df8d9/config/crd/serving.kserve.io_inferenceservices.yaml#L952-L966) in the CRD  is used to map two very different concepts:

- how to fetch a model from a remote(S3) location
- where the model is stored in the cluster for usage

This is a leaky abstraction and is causing some limitations:

- if the S3 bucket is not read-only the model deployment is not reproducible
- it's difficult or impossible to use S3-specific options

I propose to separate the two concepts using a dedicated property in the schema (e.g. `from`) that can be used to instruct the "fetch mechanism", while `storage` can stay and be dedicated exclusively to describe the properties (path etc.) of the cluster-local version of the model.

Happy to hear more thoughts about this!

label: question
title: Overwrite pod/container args
text:
Currently kserve has the issue, that you cannot overwrite the predefined/hard-coded predictor args. E.g. if I run this triton predictor:

```yaml
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "monkey-mma"
  annotations:
    sidecar.istio.io/inject: "false"
spec:
  predictor:
    triton:
      runtimeVersion: 22.06-py3
      args: [ "--strict-model-config=false"]
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 8Gi
        requests:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 8Gi
      storageUri: "pvc://models-volume/models"
```

the args will just be **appended** - and will look like this:

```
...
    Args:
      tritonserver
      --model-store=/mnt/models
      --grpc-port=9000
      --http-port=8080
      --allow-grpc=true
      --allow-http=true
      --strict-model-config=false
...
```

It would be great to have a feature to overwrite that. I'm currently compiling triton for another architecture and do not have grpc yet so tritonserver doesn't know about `grpc-port` and `allow-grpc` flags and throws an error.

I'm aware that I can just use a custom predictor (which I'm doing at the moment), but having the possibility to overwrite would be great.

Apparently this code is responsbile for the hard coded args I guess:
https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/apis/serving/v1beta1/predictor_triton.go#L56-L61

label: feature
title: Make "propagate headers" configurable per Inference Graph instead of global
text:
Today, the headers that we can pass from IG router to it's nodes are configurable only at global level.
This was done as part of this https://github.com/kserve/kserve/issues/2289

We want to make sure that this feature is available at per IG level too instead of only being available at global level so that IG owner can decide which all headers to propagate.

```

I tested the metrics endpoint inside the pod, and it seems to be running as expected:

label: feature
title: Model Storage For Multi-Node Scaling of Large Models
text:
I work on vLLM and I am making a reference architectures that demonstrate best practices for deploying vLLM within KServe. At the moment, I am focused on recommendations for `ModelStorage`.

Given the size of the models (e.g. 70B Llama is 140GB), download time is quite important for autoscaling scenarios. Additionally, in autoscaling scenarios, we often need to scale up to another GPU node, since the model typically uses an entire node (since we need at 4xA100-80GB just to serve the 70B model which will consume all the gpu resources of a node).

As a result, I am trying to design an architecture that enables me to download a model once and then mount the model to each pod as they pop up. 

I really like the OCI user flow (described at https://kserve.github.io/website/0.12/modelserving/storage/oci/), but I was unsure of whether the model assets can be shared across nodes or just within a single node, as it seems like the modelcar container needs to run on a specific node to be accessed by the `InferenceService`:

> As you can see, the Pod has now one additional container. This container is running the modelcar image and runs a ln -s /proc/$$/root/models /mnt/ command to create a symbolic link on a shared empty volume that is mounted on /mnt in the modelcar container and the serving runtime container. The magic here is the symbolic link over proc filesystem, which is shared among all containers. This is possible on Kubernetes for the container's of a Pod if the field .spec.shareProcessNamespace is set to true, which is the case for all storageUri that leverages the oci:// schema.

So, I was wondering:
- Does the OCI image use flow support caching the model weights across nodes?
- If not, is there any plan to expand this OCI image flow to support this?
- If both no, is the best pathway for something like I am describe to use PVCs with `ReadOnly` access method?

[Optional, start with the short-form [RFC template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UcBeLfZ_JMGpVrPJmYtEIVH_9Y4U3AEKQdq_IKuOMrU) to outline your ideas and get early feedback.]
[Required, use the longer-form [design doc template](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Mtoui_PP2a9N59NjYHnsvrdJ8t2iKFwIJAx1zRO_I1c) to specify and discuss your design in more detail]

label: feature
title: Check if poetry lockfile is up to date with pyproject.toml in CI environment
text: Sometimes, contributors fail to update the lock file after modifying the pyproject.toml, resulting in an obsolete lockfile.. So the tests will run against the old dependencies which may introduce subtle bugs. Poetry merely displays a warning that the lockfile is out of date, which is easily overlooked among the pile of logs in the CI environment. So we should add a test to check if the poetry lock file is up to date with pyproject.toml. This can be acheived by using `poetry lock --check` command.

label: bug
title: Transformers don't deploy with ModelMesh InferenceService in RawDeployment mode
text:
When defining an InferenceService with the modelmesh annotation it's suppose to be able to handle transformers by delegating the reconciling of it to the kserve controller instead of the modelmesh serving one. One issue I'm hitting is that it is currently only working if the underlying deployment mode is `Serverless` and not `RawDeployment`. This appears to be only a problem of the logic "falling through" an if statement here: https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/controller/v1beta1/inferenceservice/components/transformer.go#L171

Since the inferenceService is using ModeMesh as it's deployment mode, it's not covered in the check for creating the service for the transformer. That seems to be a mistake and not intentional as there's no hard dependency to using serverless for modelmesh.

Instead the controller should fall back on the `defaultDeploymentMode` entry in the configmap to figure out which deployment mode should be used to create the transformer deployment and services.

Transformers should not try and create a knative service when using a ModelMesh predictor and KServe is deployed using RawDeployment mode. 

```
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/deploymentMode: ModelMesh
  name: resnet
  namespace: kserve
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: onnx
      name: ""
      storage:
        key: localMinIO
        path: resnet
  transformer:
    containers:
      - --model_name
      - resnet
      - --predictor_protocol
      - grpc-v2
      command:
      - python
      - -m
      - custom_transformer.model_grpc
      image: custom-image-transformer-grpc:v0.1.5
      name: kserve-container
      ports:
      - containerPort: 8081
        name: h2c
        protocol: TCP
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 2Gi
        requests:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 2Gi
```

I've got a working fix locally that I will create a PR for and attach to this issue shortly.

text:
Since [ISVCs will start supporting SSEs](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/issues/2788), so we will need to add support for SSE in IG router as well as such LLMs (think of fine tuned LLMs hosted as ISVC) can and will be made part of IGs as nodes.

This needs change to start supporting more content types.

text: I tried deploying the example Triton [torchscript-cifar model](https://github.com/kserve/website/blob/main/docs/modelserving/v1beta1/triton/torchscript/torchscript.yaml) with logging enabled as per [these instructions](https://kserve.github.io/website/0.9/modelserving/logger/logger/#create-an-inferenceservice-with-logger). Evidence pointing to this being an isolated Triton issue: - If I deploy the same model *without* the logger, the model returns the expected output. - If I deploy the [example Iris model ](https://kserve.github.io/website/modelserving/v1beta1/sklearn/v2/#deploy-with-inferenceservice)(which uses the sklearn backend) *with* the logger, it also works fine. I expect making a request to the model to return the same output with or without logging enabled using the Triton backend. ``` apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1" kind: "InferenceService" metadata: name: "torchscript-cifar-logger" namespace: "kubeflow-ml" spec: predictor: logger: mode: all url: http://message-dumper.kubeflow-ml.svc.cluster.local/ triton: storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/torchscript" runtimeVersion: 21.08-py3 env: - name: OMP_NUM_THREADS value: "1" ``` The example IRIS yaml that works is: ``` apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1" kind: "InferenceService" metadata: name: "sklearn-irisv2" namespace: "kubeflow-ml" spec: predictor: logger: mode: all url: http://message-dumper.kubeflow-ml.svc.cluster.local/ sklearn: protocolVersion: "v2" storageUri: "gs://seldon-models/sklearn/iris" ``` - Knative Version: 0.23.3 - KServe Version: 0.7.0 - Kubeflow version: 1.5 - Cloud Environment:[k8s_istio/istio_dex/gcp_basic_auth/gcp_iap/aws/aws_cognito/ibm] - Kubernetes version: (use `kubectl version`): 1.21

label: feature
title: Make transformer preprocess API consistent between gRPC and HTTP protocols
text: The [_http_predict](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/model.py#L254) and [_grpc_predict](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/model.py#L289) methods should return the same data type so that we don't need to handle different data types in the `preprocess` method. If we return an `InferResponse` from both internal predict methods then the `preprocess` method does not need to be protocol-aware.

label: question
title: Authentication setup interfering with kfserving
text:
How authentication is supposed to interact with kfserving?

I followed this article to setup istio/dex authentication here:
https://journal.arrikto.com/kubeflow-authentication-with-istio-dex-5eafdfac4782

And it has been working great. However, we are trying to get kfserving to work and now the envoy filter below is interfering with it.

apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: authn-filter
spec:
  workloadLabels:
    istio: ingressgateway
  filters:
      httpService:
        serverUri:
          uri: http://authservice.istio-system.svc.cluster.local
          cluster: outbound|8080||authservice.istio-system.svc.cluster.local
        authorizationRequest: 
          allowedHeaders:
            patterns:
            - exact: "cookie"
    filterName: envoy.ext_authz
    filterType: HTTP
    listenerMatch:
      portNumber: 443
      listenerType: GATEWAY

We are trying to simply make serving api calls pass this filter all together, so I'm trying to see how I can scope down when this filter applies.

For example the call below (making a backend prediction api call) shouldn't go through this filter:
curl -v -H "Host: sklearn-iris.foo.example.com" http://localhost:8080/v1/models/sklearn-iris:predict -d @https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kubeflow/kfserving/master/docs/samples/sklearn/iris-input.json

Ideally we want a mechanism to say if the host header is "sklearn-iris.foo.example.com", then pass the authentication filter...

Looks to me kfserving is using the same kubeflow-gateway and thus the filter will apply no matter what, which seems wrong.

So just in general, how is this kfserving configuration supposed to be compatible with the recommended UI authentication setup/filter indicated above?

label: bug
title: Controller out-of-memory kill when cluster has too many secrets
text:
Given a cluster with a high count of Secrets (in the order of about 8k secrets), when and ISVC is reconciled the KServe controller tries to load into memory all Secrets in the cluster. Because the high count of Secrets, the KServe controller will reach its memory limit and the cluster will kill the pod. The cluster may re-create the pod but, given unchanged conditions, the pod will be killed continuously.

KServe controller should work fine even if the cluster has a high count of Secrets.

Not relevant. Any ISVC will lead to the crash.

On a quick code review, looks like KServe catches the secrets when using an informer/watch. However, KServe may not need to watch for changes in Secrets and, apparently, Secrets are always queried by name. If this is true, it may be better to query directly the API Server rather than via a cache of the Secrets, preventing the need of an Informer/watch.

- KServe Version: 0.11.2 - should also happen in  `master`

title: Separate timeoutSeconds to two different properties, terminationGracePeriod and request timeout.
text:
A property ‘timeoutSeconds’ engages in two features, terminationGracePeriod, request timeout.
TerminationGracePeriod and Request timeout have nothing in common. However they are controlled in same property, timeoutSeconds, which does not make sense. 

Setting timeoutSeconds to a large number makes a pod terminating for a long time.
On the other hand, lots of 504 response occurs by setting it to a small number.

I'd like to suggest to separate timeoutSends into two independent property such as terminationGracePeriod and requestTimeout

I expected that this would work, as the model was successfully downloaded and loaded. But I did find a tmp workaround below and I think I know where the issue is!

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1

metadata:
  name: huggingface
spec:

    serviceAccountName: huggingface-sa

      - --model_dir=s3://kserve-test-models/classifier
      - --tensor_input_names=input_ids
      image: kserve/huggingfaceserver:latest
      name: kserve-container

label: question
title: Question: Kubeflow installation's ingress gateway for kfserving is different than an independent install - which gateway to document in kfserving docs?
text:
The patch for 1.0.1 Kubeflow manifests now makes the ingress gateway used for prediction for Kubeflow KFServing to be `kfserving-gateway` instead of `istio-ingressgateway`.
kubeflow/manifests#1017

Refer Issues:
#668
#924

Whereas when we install kfserving independently without the help of kubeflow/manifests we still route the requests through `istio-ingressgateway`.

The current documentation refers to the `istio-ingressgateway` as the gateway for prediction requests.

An example is shown here:

https://github.com/kubeflow/kfserving/blob/master/docs/samples/tensorflow/README.md#run-a-prediction

```
CLUSTER_IP=$(kubectl -n istio-system get service istio-ingressgateway -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
```

Whether should we refer to `kfserving-gateway` or `istio-ingressgateway` in the docs?

label: feature
title: Is path-based serving supported?
text:
Hello everyone!

I see that the current way to serve `KServe` models is host-based. That is, the URL of a model looks something like this:
- `http://<model-name>-<namespace>.<domain>`.

This way, one needs to create a DNS record and a certificate for the sub-domain `<model-name>-<namespace>` where the model is hosted.

So, my question is: _is there an alternative way? A **path-based way**?_.

In that case, one should not bother about DNS records and certificates. The URL of the model could look something like this:
- `http://<domain>/<namespace>/<model-name>`

I couldn't find any issues with a similar question. Is something like this currently supported?

If not, then what are the difficulties of such a feature?

label: feature
title: Make model type + version support more specific in Serving Runtimes and add auto-placement for models with no versions
text:
Currently, the model type + version support for Serving Runtimes (SR) is not limited to a specific version. For example, a SR with following would support tensorflow models with either version 1 or no version numbers.
    name: tensorflow
    version: "1"
Another SR with following would support tensorflow models with either version 2 or no version numbers.
    name: tensorflow
    version: "2"
When a tensorflow model comes in with no specific version, it could be placed to run on either SR, potentially producing different results.

Suppose a new SR is developed later this year to support only tensorflow 3 (I know not there yet :). Since there is no way to limit a SR to a specific version, an older tensorflow model with no specific version would fail in this SR.

Most of current example models have just model type, no specific versions. So this implied no version support will cause issues later when there are newer SRs for new framework versions.

I would like to suggest to make the SR supported model format more specific. And provide better solution for models with no specific versions. Here are a few potential changes/additions...

1. add "pinToVersion" flag, this alone won't solve the random SR pick issue
2. remove the implied no version support, so the supported model formats are limited to the version in the entry, and if a version is not provided, the SR supports all versions
3. add logic to place a model on the SR that supports the latest framework version when the model has no version and there are multiple SRs supporting the target framework

Would love to get feedback and collectively come up with best solution. Thanks!

text:
It would be nice to have multiple versions of a given model flavour available to more easily test out roll out approaches. I.e. provide 2-3 artifacts on and update the documentation to show their uri. for the `sklearn` flavour, that could be something like:

```
storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model_v1"
storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model_v2"
storageUri: "gs://kfserving-examples/models/sklearn/1.0/model_v3"
```

Using these models that behave identically w.r.t input and output formats across the versions would make testing out different model versioning and rollout techniques more convenient.

label: question
title: KServe throughput (RPS) do not perform well on GPU nodes (compared to directly run in Triton)
text:
It is a resnet model (https://github.com/keras-team/keras-applications/blob/master/keras_applications/resnet50.py)
- Exported to tensorRT and served in Triton-pytorch backend via KServe 0.8. 
- The input size is 7.3M. it is ~240M/s but we are running test inside aws cluster, the bandwidth should be enough.
- Have scaled up the traffic path 4CPUs queue-proxy + 3CPUs istio-proxy + 6CPUs IGW which is able to support 10k+ qps load test (using CPU).

I observed: 
- the same deployment on the same GPU node, sending request via KServe endpoint (even it is directly sent to the http://<nodeIP>:8080/v2/models/resnet50/infer) vs directly to triton (ssh in the container and send to http://localhost:8080/v2/models/resnet50/infer), the RPS has HUGE difference: 50 vs 120.
- Low GPU, CPU utilization in KServe, GPU is always < 20%. If directly run in Triton, the GPU utilization can be 50% or higher. It seems CPU usage is capped when sending to KServe, no matter how many CPUs we allocated to Triton, and no matter how many traffic we sent to the KServe endpoint, the CPU usage is ~3 CPUs.
- KServe has much lower latency (9.39ms vs 73.5ms)
- Queue-proxy and istio-proxy utilization is really low too, < 0.5CPU (and we have scaled up both).

KServe should have same QPS as Triton for GPU nodes. For **CPU** models, I tested KServe performs exactly the same as Triton.

title: Question on Canary deployment of InferenceService
text:
As discussed in [this](https://kserve.github.io/website/0.9/modelserving/v1beta1/rollout/canary-example/#canary-rollout-example) example of canary rollout, user needs to carry out three steps:
1. Update the InferenceService by adding the canaryTrafficPercent field to the predictor component
2. After rolling out the canary model, Run Prediction to ensure no failure happens with new deployment
3. Promote the canary model by removing the canaryTrafficPercent field and re-applying the InferenceService custom resource

label: question

text:

In my work, I often encounter very large test data. Since kfserving cannot perform inferences on massive amounts of data at one time, I have to split the test data into smaller data sets and store them in json. I also notice that the number of json files does not seem to be a critical factor. Even if the number of json files is small, but the json file contains a lot of data, you will get the same error.         cluster_ip = service.spec.cluster_ip

            cluster_ip = service.status.load_balancer.ingress[0].hostname
        else:
            cluster_ip = service.status.load_balancer.ingress[0].ip

if __name__ == '__main__':

label: feature
title: Make MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH Configurable for Image Input Size Flexibility
text:
I would like to request a new feature that allows the `MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH` in the `GRPCServer` class to be configurable. Currently, it is hard-coded to `8388608` (8 MB), which imposes a limitation on the size of image inputs that can be processed via gRPC.  in `kserve/protocol/grpc/server.py`

```python
MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 8388608

class GRPCServer:
    def __init__(self, port: int, data_plane: DataPlane, model_repository_extension: ModelRepositoryExtension):
        self._port = port
        self._data_plane = data_plane
        self._model_repository_extension = model_repository_extension
        self._server = None

    async def start(self, max_workers):
        inference_servicer = InferenceServicer(self._data_plane, self._model_repository_extension)
        self._server = aio.server(
            futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers),
            interceptors=(LoggingInterceptor(),),
            options=[
                ("grpc.max_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
                ("grpc.max_send_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
                ("grpc.max_receive_message_length", MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH),
            ],
        )
```
---

The fixed MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH value limits the ability to send larger payloads, such as **high-resolution images**, through gRPC. This restriction can hinder use cases where larger input sizes are necessary for model inference.

I am willing to implement this feature and submit a pull request if approved. Please let me know if this approach aligns with the project’s goals and if there are any specific guidelines I should follow.

I think we need to change `MAX_GRPC_MESSAGE_LENGTH` as configurable through [GRPCServer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/grpc/server.py#L32) -> [ModelServer](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L66) -> [argparse](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/af54048e126ec302251933bcd260154a75a33b1e/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L41) -> ServingRuntime.

Thank you for considering this enhancement.

label: bug
title: InferenceService Deployments cannot scale beyond 1 replica due to Reconciliation
text:
`InferenceService` Deployments fail to autoscale beyond 1 replica if other non-kserve controllers inject labels/annotations in deployment after it is deployed.

When deploying an `InferenceService` in `RawDeployment` mode:
1. KServe controller-manager creates the set of resources for the KServe application (Deployment, Service, HPA)
2. After the Deployment is created, another non-kserve controller adds its labels and annotations.
3. This annotation/label injection triggers Deployment Reconciliation.
4. The reconciled change is immediately overwritten by the non-kserve controller which re-adds its labels/annotations.
5. Step 3 occurs, preventing deployments from scaling beyond 1 replica.

1. KServe to ignore non-KServe labels and annotations during the Deployment Reconciliation process.
2. The ability to configure which parts of the `DeploymentSpec` are ignored for the purposes of Reconciliation e.g.`“Template.Spec.ServiceAccountName”`

We have an in-house patch which solves this issue by addressing the points above, which involves only considering KServe annotations and labels during reconciliation and adding more fields to the ignored fields during comparison.

- Istio Version: 1.14.1
- KFServing Version: 0.9.0

label: feature
title: Handle Knative Autoscaler Configuration When Creating Knative Services
text:
Currently, Kserve does not take into account the knative autoscaler configuration when creating knative services for Inference Services or Inference Graphs. This leads to several gaps in the way kserve handles the creation of knative services:

1. kserve does not account for the global knative configuration of `initial-scale`. This can lead to scenarios where the number of replicas created to initialize a knative revision does not fall into the range of the requested min or max replicas for the Inference Service or Inference Graph. Consider the following scenarios:

    1. knative is globally configured with an `initial-scale` value that exceeds the max replicas requested for an Inference Service or Inference Graph. In this scenario, the knative revision created will be initialized with a greater number of replicas created than what the user requested as the maximum value.
    2. knative is globally configured with an `initial-scale` value that exceeds the min replicas requested for an Inference Service, but is less than the requested max replicas. knative will always choose the larger of `min-scale` and `initial-scale` as the initial target scale for a knative revision. So, in this scenario the knative revision created will be initialized with a greater number of replicas created than the user requested minimum value. A prominent case of this scenario would be when the min replicas requested is 0. The default `initial-scale` value used by knative is 1, so if a user installs knative and kserve out of the box, there will always be 1 replica created to initialize the revision when min replicas 0 is requested.

2. kserve only [adds](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/pkg/controller/v1beta1/inferenceservice/reconcilers/knative/ksvc_reconciler.go#L92) the knative `autoscaling.knative.dev/max-scale` annotation to a knative service's template spec if the max replicas value requested for an Inference Service is a non zero value (**kserve never adds this annotation for Inference Graphs**). Due to this, if an Inference Service is requested with 0 max replicas, knative will use the globally configured `max-scale` value for the created knative revision, alternatively for Inference Graphs, the globally configured `max-scale` value will **always** be used. This presents a bug for the following scenario:

    1. knative is globally configured with a `max-scale-limit` value of 0, i.e. infinite scaling is allowed, and a `max-scale` value that is greater than 0. If a user desires to allow a requested Inference Service or Inference Graph to scale up infiinitely by requesting for the max replicas to be 0, this would not be possible since no `autoscaling.knative.dev/max-scale`  annotation is added, knative will fall back to using the global configuration which has a `max-scale` value that is greater than 0, effectively placing a limit on the scale.

The scenarios mentioned in [1] above, while still leading to a confusing user experience, can be argued as the proper behavior a defined by knative. It is up to debate whether these represent gaps that should be addressed. On the other hand, the scenario mentioned in [2] above presents a possible bug. That being said, I have worked on implementing solutions for all scenarios mentioned above, which are listed below:

1.i. When a knative service is created for an Inference Service or Inference Graph, read the  knative autoscaler configuration defined in the knativeserving custom resource to get the `initial-scale` value. If the requested max replicas is greater than 0 and less than the configured `initial-scale` value, then add the `autoscaling.knative.dev/initial-scale` annotation to the created knative service's template spec with a value equal to the requested max replicas. Alternatively, we can output a log in the kserve-controller-manager pod to inform the user that the globally configured knative initial scale value exceeds the requested max replicas.

1.ii. When a knative service is crea …[truncated]

label: feature
title: Enhancing KServe Model Fetching with oci: Schema and Sidecar Containers
text:
I propose an enhancement for model fetching in KServe using an `oci:` schema for model location. Currently, an init container fetches the model data from a location specified by a URL within the `InferenceService`. This process, however, has several limitations, especially for large models. This proposal aims to reduce startup latency, minimize local disk storage waste, and offer easier optimization methods by fetching the model directly from an OCI image stored in node-local image storage. 

The proposed model setup involves:
1. Adopting an `oci:` URL schema as a reference to the model in an `InferenceService`. 
2. Using a sidecar container, instead of an init-container, added to the Knative Service to hold the actual model. This allows the model to be fully contained and distributed within an OCI image.
3. Configuring the overall Pod as `shareProcessNamespace: true` to ensure all sidecars can access each other's filesystem via `/proc/<pid>/root`. This way, the main container can directly access the model from the data-container.

This approach could provide several benefits, including:
- Reduced local disk space usage as pods running the same model on a node will access the same directory containing the model.
- Lower startup times due to the elimination of copying potentially large data.
- Ability to leverage known techniques to pre-fetch container images to nodes or use lazy-loading techniques (e.g., with the [stargz snapshotter for containerd](https://github.com/containerd/stargz-snapshotter)).
- Resolution of certain problems encountered with init-containers when using the [init-container with Istio's CNI plugin](https://istio.io/latest/docs/setup/additional-setup/cni/#compatibility-with-application-init-containers).

If the community agrees, I would be keen to work on implementing a Proof of Concept (PoC) to measure the benefits of this approach. I appreciate any feedback and look forward to our discussion.

title: MIG support for huggingface runtime
text:
From my understanding, KServe currently does not support running models on multi-instance GPUs, but the upstream vLLM seems to support it. Something like this won't work:

```yaml
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: multilingual-e5-large-instruct
spec:
  predictor:
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: huggingface
      args:
        - --model_name=multilingual-e5-large-instruct
        - --model_id=intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct
      resources:
        limits:
          nvidia.com/mig-1g.12gb: "2"
      env:
        - name: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: "0"
```

There are no explicit error messages, but the InferenceService fails to create any workloads (Pods/Deployments/ReplicaSets). Maybe a validating webhook does not allow this (see [allowed constants](https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/ae964630d9c480af199e2bfa77fb99d47915048f/pkg/constants/constants.go#L246), for example), maybe this is a much more complicated problem, I am ufortunately not familiar with KServe architecture.

That being said, this vLLM-based solution will work:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: vllm-e5-mig
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: vllm-e5
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: vllm-e5
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: vllm
        image: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.9.0.1
        command:
        - "python3"
        - "-m"
        - "vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server"
        - "--model"
        - "intfloat/multilingual-e5-large-instruct"
        - "--port=8000"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8000
        resources:
          limits:
            nvidia.com/mig-1g.12gb: 1
        env:
        - name: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES
          value: "0"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: vllm-e5-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: vllm-e5
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8000
  type: ClusterIP 
```

Would be nice to run a similar setup with huggingface ClusterServingRuntime.

label: feature
title: Improve InferenceService status
text:
https://github.com/kserve/modelmesh-serving/blob/main/docs/predictors/inferenceservice-cr.md

> conditions - Various condition entries. Pertinent entries are:
>
> PredictorReady: predictor readiness condition. Status is true when the predictor's endpoints are ready to serve inferencing requests. Note that this does not necessarily mean requests will respond immediately, the corresponding model may or may not be loaded in memory. In the case that it isn't there may be some delay before the response comes back.
>
> Ready: aggregated condition of all conditions.

The “Ready” status is confusing. The model can be callable when the `PredictorReady` is False. What are the `conditions` here? What does `PredictorReady` mean? Is Predictor CR still used or is it just a legacy way of calling things? It would be nice if there is a way distinguish if the model has some non-retriable error like the wrong file path, or if it’s just temporarily not loaded due to lack of usage and can be available when called. 

Talking with @yuzisun, he suggests that
> currently it is really reflecting the “model deployment status”  as your active model is still callable but the target model deployment may fail.

Rename the current Status to "model deployment status", and have something to indicate the current model's status. Right now I think it's just the activeModelState. 

Since
> Upon creation, the active model status of an InferenceService will always transition to Loaded state (unless the loading fails), but later if unused, it is possible that the active model status ends up in a Standby state which means the model is still available to serve requests but the first request could incur a loading delay. 

Use activeModelState in combination with lastFailureInfo, if a model has been loaded before, it shouldn't have any lastFailureInfo.

label: feature
title: KServe REST Server doesn't check model readiness before attempting inference.
text:
As of now, it's possible to perform inference over a `Model` when the model is not in the ready state.
Neither the V1, nor V2 REST endpoints check whether `Model.ready` has been set before attempting inference:
- https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/236c1dcff60a4932b4db28c6cec9ce6b1dc470f0/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v1_endpoints.py#L55
- https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/236c1dcff60a4932b4db28c6cec9ce6b1dc470f0/python/kserve/kserve/protocol/rest/v2_endpoints.py#L130

I understand that it's expected that the client checks the separate readiness endpoint before sending inference requests, and that the InferenceService itself should not be marked as ready in Kubernetes until the readiness endpoint returns 200, but I think the inference endpoints should raise `ModelNotReady` themselves when appropriate.

Is there a principled reason for not including this that I'm not aware of? Happy to make a PR to fix this if it's deemed necessary. 

This caused an issue in our deployed environment, where one client which checked the readiness endpoint was failing on a deployed inference service, but another client which did not check the readiness was returning successful predictions, which caused a lot of confusion until we realised we'd forgotten to set the `.ready` flag on our `Model`.

label: feature
title: Support .json and .ubj model format for XGBoost server image
text:
In the XGBoost image, the only supported model format is .bst: https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/56b8fe0d189fc0d557e9a8af07eab0c12852d5fd/python/xgbserver/xgbserver/model.py#L28

This format has been deprecated for a while and is not backwards compatible between xgboost framework versions. The recommended model format is .json or .ubj: https://xgboost.readthedocs.io/en/stable/tutorials/saving_model.html

Users that want to use the recommended model format for XGBoost models, are currently not able to do so.

Support the recommended file formats, while also keeping support for the old .bst format.

title: Cloud events responses need to be configurable for custom predictors and transformers
text:

Currently it returns the same Ce-Type and Ce-Source, which means that the transformer/predictor will get those events again except this time without the proper payload, at any case they need to be configurable so the proper consumer can pick them up. 

I already have an example how this should be done but I am unsure how to allow for configuration view the custom spec. Should this be env variables? 

https://github.com/pwc-labs/kfserving/blob/ce-time-fix/python/kfserving/kfserving/handlers/http.py#L85

Also note that: RFC 3339 is not compatible with ISO. I corrected this as well. 

```python
self.set_header('ce-time', datetime.utcnow().replace(tzinfo=pytz.utc).trftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))
````

Reading the documentation posted [here](https://kserve.github.io/website/0.10/modelserving/storage/s3/s3/), it shows that I can either annotate the `Secret`  or the `ServiceAccount` (in the case of using an existing secret).  If the endpoint annotations can _only_ be used on the secret (in the non IRSA mode), then this might be a documentation fix until this feature can be implemented.

Deployed this bit

<details><summary>Deployed with</summary>

```yaml
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: app
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: minio
  namespace: app
type: Opaque
stringData:
  AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: abcd1234
  AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: admin
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3aware
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: "minio.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "0"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-region: "us-east-2"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-useanoncredential: "false"
secrets:
  - name: minio
---
apiVersion: "serving.kserve.io/v1beta1"
kind: "InferenceService"
metadata:
  name: "sklearn-irisv2"
  namespace: app
spec:
  predictor:
    serviceAccountName: s3aware
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: sklearn
      runtime: kserve-mlserver
      storageUri: "s3://models"
```

</details>

  AWS_ENDPOINT_URL: "minio.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: s3aware
  namespace: app
  annotations:
    serving.kserve.io/s3-endpoint: "minio.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-usehttps: "0"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-region: "us-east-2"
    serving.kserve.io/s3-useanoncredential: "false"
secrets:
  - name: minio
  - name: minio-endpoint
```

</details>

title: New model deployments are missing virtualServices
text:

label: bug
title: Support for v2 inference request of datatype bytes in HTTP
text:
With the earlier tornado web server the data field with `string` input and datatype `BYTES` was considered valid. Example - https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/samples/v1beta1/torchserve/v2/bytes_conv/mnist_v2_bytes.json

WIth current FastAPI server, the validator expects the data field to be a list. 

From the docs there is no example for representing bytes datatype in v2 protocol inference request. So what is the recommended way of sending the bytesarray for HTTP request ?

- Cloud Environment:[k8s_istio/istio_dex/gcp_basic_auth/gcp_iap/aws/aws_cognito/ibm]

label: feature
title: Support speculative decoding in vLLM backend of HuggingFace server
text:
KServe needs a way to supply the `speculative_model` in addition to `model` when instantiating the `vllm.LLM` object. An example:

```
llm = LLM(
    model="facebook/opt-6.7b",
    tensor_parallel_size=1,
    speculative_model="facebook/opt-125m",
    num_speculative_tokens=5,
    use_v2_block_manager=True,
)
```

The current vLLM backend in HuggingFace server does not support this additional parameter yet.

Reference: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/models/spec_decode.html#speculating-with-a-draft-model

label: question
title: Question about kafka message delivery to model handler
text:
Please excuse my limited knowledge on kserve and kafka. Looking into the kafka example https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/samples/kafka I had difficulty understanding how kafka source https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/docs/samples/kafka/kafka-source.yaml is able to deliver cloudevent to PredictHandler https://github.com/kserve/kserve/blob/master/python/kserve/kserve/model_server.py#L84. As far as I understand the model name is parsed from the url path. I could not find out how kafka source is configured to deliver the message to the predict handler of the right model.

I would appreciate any pointers or explanations. 

Kafka source is configured with a uri that matching the protocol version and model name that model is served with.

- Kfdef:[k8s_istio/istio_dex/gcp_basic_auth/gcp_iap/aws/aws_cognito/ibm]
